note: Rewritten from Sands' (1999) new species description, original in English; the genus lacks soldiers, only the worker and the alate are distinguishable, and the original gives a complete description only for the worker, so only the worker is listed; measurements follow the original ranges, mean/SD not listed individually; locality, type specimens and etymology not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Distinguished from the closely related A. gasteruptus only by the shorter apical spines of the primary rows of the enteric valve and the more clearly outlined scales of the secondary rows, the symmetry tending towards bilateral rather than clearly three-radiate. From A. camerunensis it differs in that the latter has the fourth marginal tooth of the left mandible just touching the lateral edge of the molar prominence, a longer fore tibia, and a six-radiate enteric valve with large, straight conical spines. From A. congoensis it differs in that the latter has the third distal spur of the fore tibia reduced, the third lobe of the enteric valve seat nearly as large as the outer pair, the apical spines of the primary rows generally longer, and the ridges closer to three-radiate.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow or yellow, the darkest part of the antennal flagellum yellow or pale yellowish brown, pronotum and legs yellowish white, abdominal tergites transparent. Head capsule short-oval, nearly circular, setae numerous but not dense, projecting, the longest setae scattered at random. Fontanelle absent. Fore coxa without conspicuous stout setae, or with 4 or more stout setae on the anterior surface arranged in rows or groups; fore tibia with 3 distal spurs, the third well developed, at least one-half the length of the others. Left mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than the posterior margin or nearly equilateral, anterior margin of the third marginal tooth shorter than or equal to that of the first marginal tooth, the proximal end of the fourth marginal tooth not touching the molar prominence in frontal view; right mandible: anterior margin of the first marginal tooth equal to or shorter than that of the second marginal tooth. Measurements: head width 0.565—0.717 mm; pronotum width 0.375—0.495 mm, length 0.169—0.293 mm; hind tibia length 0.565—0.706 mm; fore tibia length 0.489—0.556 mm; left mandible index 0.697—1.144, right mandible index 0.879—1.278.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The midgut–hindgut junction arises ventrally below the nerve cord or to its right; the first hindgut segment is rather short, tubular throughout, up to 8 times as long as its proximal width; in the undissected abdomen the enteric valve lies to the right of the heart (dorsal view) or to the left of the nerve cord (ventral view); the third lobe of the enteric valve seat is smaller than the outer pair. The enteric valve ridges are markedly waisted at the base of the apical spines and then widen, the ends of the ridges sclerotized, pale brown or yellowish brown; the primary rows bear very long tapering spines, ridges one and four with at most 1—14, ridge two with 1—9, ridge three with 10—20, the symmetry nearly three-radiate, the intercalary ridges reduced; the longest spines straight or curved but evenly tapering, not wider than the narrowest point of ridge three; the secondary rows bear sparser, conspicuous spines scattered on one or more ridges, lengthening towards the ridge apex; the membrane between and outside the ridges bears scales and minute spines, denser at the apex, with marginal scales proximally.
